w: Dedicated to Saint Peter and a monument historique since 1906, this is the seat of the Archbishop of Rennes, Dol and Saint-Malo -- three dioceses folded into one address. The building anchors the old town it has watched rebuild itself around, stone by stone, ever since.
s: Seat of the archbishop, in one building
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral dedicated to Saint Peter
seat of the Archbishop of Rennes, Dol, and Saint-Malo
monument historique since 1906

w: Its first exhibits were confiscated during the Revolution in 1794 -- the seed of a collection that has tracked Brittany from prehistory to the present ever since. Housed from 1815 alongside the fine-arts museum in the old Palais universitaire, it moved into the Champs Libres centre in 2006.
s: A Breton history museum born of revolutionary loot
_facts: social history museum in the Champs Libres cultural centre
first collection items came from confiscations in 1794 during the French Revolution
housed alongside the Museum of Fine Arts from 1815, moved to present site in 2006

w: Founded before the 11th century and dedicated to Our Lady of Miracles and Virtues, this church earned its title the hard way -- 14th- and 18th-century events called miraculous fed a cult of Mary strong enough to win it basilica status in 1916. Look for the wrought-iron pulpit and the ex-votos.
s: A church elevated to basilica after reported miracles
_facts: founded before the 11th century, dedicated to Our Lady of Miracles and Virtues
14th- and 18th-century events described as miraculous grew a strong Marian cult here
elevated to minor basilica in 1916; notable for its wrought-iron pulpit and ex-votos

w: Inaugurated in 1836 in the Italian style, this opera house faces Rennes' town hall across the Place de la Mairie -- a civic face-off in stone. Still staging opera today, plus the open-air "Opera en plein air" each summer, and listed as a historic monument since 1975.
s: Italian-style opera house facing the town hall
_facts: Italian-style opera house designed by Charles Millardet, inaugurated 1836
stands on Place de la Mairie opposite the town hall
listed as a historic monument since 29 October 1975

w: Rennes burned in 1720, and this grand hotel rose from the ashes in 1728, its architect said to be Jacques Gabriel. Home for two centuries to the earls of Blossac, then to Brittany's military commander, it later gave the novelist Paul Feval his birthplace. Now state-owned, it houses the region's cultural affairs office.
s: An 18th-century mansion built after Rennes' great fire
_facts: 18th-century hotel particulier built 1728 after the 1720 fire that destroyed much of Rennes
residence of the earls of Blossac, then of Brittany's commander in chief
novelist Paul Feval was born here; state-owned since 1982, houses cultural affairs offices

w: Formed in 1990 from the merger of two older companies, this theatre earned the nickname "the Great Eight" for the shape of its building. It became a European centre for dance and theatre production in 2002, and every November throws open its stage for the Festival du TNB.
s: A theatre nicknamed the 'Great Eight' for its shape
_facts: established 1990 by combining Centre dramatique de l'Ouest and Maison de la Culture of Rennes
nicknamed the 'Great Eight' for its building's shape
became a European centre of dance and theatre production in 2002; hosts the annual Festival du TNB

w: From ancient Egyptian antiquities to modern art, this municipal collection spans further than its modest size suggests -- widely ranked among the most important fine-arts museums in France outside the capital, especially for its paintings and drawings.
s: A fine-art museum ranked outside Paris' top tier
_facts: municipal museum of fine arts, collections from ancient Egypt to modern art
considered one of the most important fine-arts museums in France outside Paris
notable for its holdings of paintings and drawings
